atoms.text: This guide configures access for the FrameForge transcoding service, which reads mezzanine video files and writes HLS renditions. The S3 bucket media-masters-prod and the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role both belong to account 111122223333. The service reads source files from the prefix incoming/ and writes segments and playlists to the prefix renditions/. Access is granted only through the identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Add a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod with an s3:prefix condition limited to incoming/, so the service can enumerate pending files. Because the role and the bucket share an account, an allow in the identity-based policy is sufficient unless another policy explicitly denies the request. After attaching the policy, start a test job that points at one file under incoming/. Confirm that the playlist and segment objects appear under renditions/ and that the job log reports no AccessDenied responses.

This guide configures access for the FrameForge transcoding service, which reads mezzanine video files and writes HLS renditions. The S3 bucket media-masters-prod is owned by account 444455556666, while the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role belongs to account 111122223333. The service reads source files from the prefix incoming/ and writes segments and playlists to the prefix renditions/. The bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/frameforge-transcode-role as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/renditions/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod with an s3:prefix condition limited to incoming/. Because the request crosses an account boundary, the role's own policy in account 111122223333 must permit the same actions, but the bucket policy statement supplies the cross-account permission. After saving the policy, start a test job that points at one file under incoming/. Confirm that the playlist and segment objects appear under renditions/ and that the job log reports no AccessDenied responses.

This guide sets up access for the ScanRead OCR service, which reads scanned PDF files and writes extracted text as JSON documents. The S3 bucket records-archive-prod and the IAM role scanread-worker-role are both in account 111122223333. The service reads input from the prefix scans/ and writes one JSON object per page to the prefix text/. The grant is carried entirely by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Create a policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-prod/scans/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-prod/text/*. Attach the policy to scanread-worker-role and verify that no permissions boundary or service control policy removes these actions. Since both resources are in the same account, no principal needs to be named in any bucket-level statement. Submit a sample PDF to the scans/ prefix and wait for the job to complete. Check that the matching JSON objects are present under text/ and that their sizes are non-zero.

This guide sets up access for the ScanRead OCR service, which reads scanned PDF files and writes extracted text as JSON documents. The S3 bucket records-archive-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role scanread-worker-role is in account 111122223333. The service reads input from the prefix scans/ and writes one JSON object per page to the prefix text/. The grant is carried by the bucket policy, which the bucket owner edits to name the role as a principal. Add a statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/scanread-worker-role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-prod/scans/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-prod/text/*. Account 111122223333 must also allow these actions in the role's policy, because cross-account requests need approval on both sides. Set Object Ownership on the bucket to bucket owner enforced so that written objects belong to account 444455556666. Submit a sample PDF to the scans/ prefix and wait for the job to complete. Check that the matching JSON objects are present under text/ and that their sizes are non-zero.

This guide describes how to let the PixelTile image service create thumbnails from original photographs. The S3 bucket photo-assets-prod and the IAM role pixeltile-resize-role belong to the same account, 111122223333. The service reads originals from the prefix originals/ and writes 256-pixel and 512-pixel JPEG thumbnails to the prefix thumbnails/. Only the role's identity-based policy grants access, and the bucket policy is left as it is. The policy statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-assets-prod/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-assets-prod/thumbnails/*. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, because the service never removes originals or existing thumbnails. A same-account allow is enough for these requests as long as no explicit deny applies to the role. Upload a test image to originals/ and invoke the service for that key. Verify that both thumbnail sizes appear under thumbnails/ with the expected content type of image/jpeg.

This guide describes how to let the PixelTile image service create thumbnails from original photographs. The S3 bucket photo-assets-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role pixeltile-resize-role is in account 111122223333. The service reads originals from the prefix originals/ and writes 256-pixel and 512-pixel JPEG thumbnails to the prefix thumbnails/. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement that names the role ARN as the principal. The statement lists arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/pixeltile-resize-role and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-assets-prod/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-assets-prod/thumbnails/*. Do not include s3:DeleteObject, because the service never removes originals or existing thumbnails. The role's policy in account 111122223333 must allow the same actions, since a cross-account request needs both sides to agree. Upload a test image to originals/ and invoke the service for that key. Verify that both thumbnail sizes appear under thumbnails/ with the expected content type of image/jpeg.

This guide covers storage access for the LoudLevel audio service, which reads raw WAV recordings and writes loudness-normalized MP3 files. The S3 bucket podcast-audio-prod and the IAM role loudlevel-batch-role are in account 111122223333. The service reads recordings from the prefix raw-audio/ and writes encoded files to the prefix normalized/. Access is provided solely by the identity-based policy on the role, so the bucket policy is not edited. Write a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio-prod/raw-audio/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio-prod/normalized/*. Add s3:AbortMultipartUpload on the normalized/ prefix, because large episodes are uploaded in multiple parts. The role and bucket share an account, so the identity-based allow takes effect without any bucket-level principal. Run the service against a single 60-minute WAV file. Confirm that the resulting MP3 object is present under normalized/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

This guide covers storage access for the LoudLevel audio service, which reads raw WAV recordings and writes loudness-normalized MP3 files. The S3 bucket podcast-audio-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role loudlevel-batch-role is in account 111122223333. The service reads recordings from the prefix raw-audio/ and writes encoded files to the prefix normalized/. Access is provided by a statement the bucket owner adds to the bucket policy with the role as the named principal. The statement uses Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/loudlevel-batch-role and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio-prod/raw-audio/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio-prod/normalized/*. Include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on the normalized/ prefix, because large episodes are uploaded in multiple parts. The role's policy in account 111122223333 must also allow these actions, as the request is evaluated in both accounts. Run the service against a single 60-minute WAV file. Confirm that the resulting MP3 object is present under normalized/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

This guide explains how to give the PageShift conversion service access to a bucket holding contract documents. The service reads DOCX files from inbox/ and writes the converted PDF files to outbox/. The S3 bucket contracts-docs-prod and the IAM role pageshift-convert-role are both in account 111122223333. The grant is made only in the identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is unchanged. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-docs-prod/inbox/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-docs-prod/outbox/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition restricting listing to the inbox/ prefix. Administrators in the account can attach this policy directly, and no external principal needs to be recognized by the bucket. Place a sample DOCX file in inbox/ and trigger a conversion job. Verify that the PDF with the same base name appears in outbox/ and that the job reports a successful status.

This guide explains how to give the PageShift conversion service access to a bucket holding contract documents. The service reads DOCX files from inbox/ and writes the converted PDF files to outbox/. The S3 bucket contracts-docs-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the service runs under the role pageshift-convert-role in account 111122223333. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement whose principal is the account ID 111122223333. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-docs-prod/inbox/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-docs-prod/outbox/*, plus s3:ListBucket restricted to the inbox/ prefix. Naming the account delegates the decision, so administrators in account 111122223333 must attach a matching identity-based policy to the role. Without that policy, no principal in that account can use the permission. Place a sample DOCX file in inbox/ and trigger a conversion job. Verify that the PDF with the same base name appears in outbox/ and that the job reports a successful status.

This guide configures bucket access for the CaptionWorks subtitle service, which reads extracted audio tracks and writes WebVTT caption files. The S3 bucket broadcast-library-prod and the IAM role captionworks-asr-role are in account 111122223333. The service reads tracks from the prefix tracks/ and writes one caption file per track to the prefix captions/. Only the role's identity-based policy carries the grant, and the bucket policy is not changed. Define a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-library-prod/tracks/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-library-prod/captions/*. Keep the resource ARNs scoped to these prefixes so that the role cannot read other content in the bucket. Because the role is in the bucket's own account, the allow is evaluated once and no bucket-level principal is needed. Submit a test track with a known transcript. Check that a .vtt object appears under captions/ and that its timestamps start at 00:00:00.000.

This guide configures bucket access for the CaptionWorks subtitle service, which reads extracted audio tracks and writes WebVTT caption files. The S3 bucket broadcast-library-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role captionworks-asr-role is in account 111122223333. The service reads tracks from the prefix tracks/ and writes one caption file per track to the prefix captions/. The bucket owner carries the grant by adding a bucket policy statement that names the role as the principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-library-prod/tracks/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-library-prod/captions/* for arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/captionworks-asr-role. Keep the resource ARNs scoped to these prefixes so that the role cannot read other content in the bucket. Because the role is in a different account, its own policy must also allow these actions, and both evaluations must succeed. Submit a test track with a known transcript. Check that a .vtt object appears under captions/ and that its timestamps start at 00:00:00.000.

This guide shows how to authorize the MarkSeal watermarking service to process design proofs. The service authenticates as the IAM user markseal-batch-user, which reads proof images and writes watermarked copies. The S3 bucket design-proofs-prod and the user are both in account 111122223333. Proofs are read from the prefix proofs/ and watermarked PNG files are written to the prefix watermarked/. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user, so the bucket policy is not touched. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::design-proofs-prod/proofs/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::design-proofs-prod/watermarked/*. Prefer attaching the policy through an IAM group if several batch users share the same duties. A same-account allow is sufficient, provided no explicit deny exists in another policy. Run the service on one proof and review the output. Verify that the watermarked file under watermarked/ has the same pixel dimensions as the source.

This guide shows how to authorize the MarkSeal watermarking service to process design proofs. The service authenticates as the IAM user markseal-batch-user, which reads proof images and writes watermarked copies. The S3 bucket design-proofs-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the user is in account 111122223333. Proofs are read from the prefix proofs/ and watermarked PNG files are written to the prefix watermarked/. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/markseal-batch-user as the principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::design-proofs-prod/proofs/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::design-proofs-prod/watermarked/*. The user's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must allow the same actions, preferably through a group shared by batch users. The two policies are evaluated together, and the request succeeds only if neither denies it. Run the service on one proof and review the output. Verify that the watermarked file under watermarked/ has the same pixel dimensions as the source.

This guide describes access for the BundlePack service, which reads finished media files and writes ZIP archives for delivery. The S3 bucket delivery-assets-prod and the IAM role bundlepack-archive-role are in account 111122223333. The service reads files from the prefix staging/ and writes each archive to the prefix bundles/. The grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy stays as it is. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::delivery-assets-prod/staging/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::delivery-assets-prod/bundles/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition for staging/, because the service enumerates all files that belong to a delivery. Archives can be several gigabytes, so include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on bundles/. Same-account access needs no principal in a bucket statement, and the identity-based allow is enough. Create a test delivery with three files in staging/ and start a bundling job. Confirm that one ZIP object appears under bundles/ and that its listing shows all three files.

This guide describes access for the BundlePack service, which reads finished media files and writes ZIP archives for delivery. The S3 bucket delivery-assets-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role bundlepack-archive-role is in account 111122223333. The service reads files from the prefix staging/ and writes each archive to the prefix bundles/. The grant is made in the bucket policy, where the bucket owner names the role ARN as the principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::delivery-assets-prod/staging/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::delivery-assets-prod/bundles/* for arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/bundlepack-archive-role. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition for staging/, and include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on bundles/ for large archives. The role's own policy in account 111122223333 must also allow these actions, as cross-account access requires both. Create a test delivery with three files in staging/ and start a bundling job. Confirm that one ZIP object appears under bundles/ and that its listing shows all three files.
